description: Web-tier coverage baseline (P1-27-QA-001). Scope is the `coverage.include` allow-list in apps/web/vitest.config.ts — the P1-27 CRM and Vehicle features, the dashboard routes that mount them, and the shared library under src/lib. Measured by `npm run test:web -- --coverage`, which runs BOTH vitest projects (`logic` in node, `dom` in jsdom) into one v8 report, because they are two environments over one application. Merging this with the unit or backend tier would overstate all three: those measure apps/api.
establishedBy: LOCAL measurement in the p1-27/core-api-boundary worktree at base 0650a506b5990a809a3f350370b16e25edb1e7fd, `npm run test --workspace @rootlco/web -- --coverage`, 1533 tests across 70 test files, 0 failed, 90 instrumented source files. This tier had NEVER been measured before: apps/web/vitest.config.ts declared two projects and no `coverage` block at all, the repository-root config's `include` list is entirely apps/api/src, and neither committed coverage baseline mentioned apps/web. So there is no hosted run to cite yet — the first hosted run of this tier is the one that replaces this field.
ciWiring: WIRED. The apps/web `test:ci` script carries the coverage flags, so the suite is executed once for both purposes, and `_reusable-node-quality.yml` runs `coverage-gate.mjs` against this baseline in the web-quality task. The flags live inside the workspace script deliberately: `npm run test:web -- --coverage` loses the separator at the second npm layer and runs a plain `vitest run`, which exits 0, writes no report, and produces a coverage job that measured nothing while calling itself a coverage run.
ciWiringTrap: DO NOT write step (1) as `npm run test:web -- --coverage`. Measured on this tree: npm appends the argument to the delegating script WITHOUT the `--` separator, so the line that actually executes is `npm run test --workspace @rootlco/web --coverage`, the inner npm swallows `--coverage` as one of its own config flags, and the command that runs is a bare `vitest run`. The suite passes, the job exits 0, no coverage report is emitted and no coverage directory is created — a green coverage job that measured nothing. The workspace-direct spelling above carries the flag through and is what every figure in this document was measured with. `npm run test:web` is still the registered command the reachability gate sees, because `check-command-coverage.mjs` follows the `--workspace` edge.
runtimeNote: Instrumentation slows the `dom` project materially. Across four coverage runs of the final tree, three reported 1505/1505 passing and one failed a single pre-existing case, `apps/web/tests/record-form-consumers.dom.test.tsx:425`, on a `getByRole` that timed out. The same case passes in every run without `--coverage`. It is a latent timing flake that v8 instrumentation makes more likely rather than a defect this measurement introduced, and it is written down here so the first red hosted run is diagnosed rather than re-discovered.
establishmentProvenance: LOCAL, PENDING A HOSTED RE-MEASUREMENT. Recorded as local rather than dressed up as hosted. Node v24.16.0 on win32, @vitest/coverage-v8 3.2.7. A hosted ubuntu-latest run may differ by fractions of a point through v8 line attribution, which is what `tolerancePercentagePoints` is for; if it differs by more than that, the hosted number is the authority and this document is corrected in a commit that says so.
measurementConventionNote: The percentages above are coverage-gate.mjs's own `pct()` — covered/total to two decimals, rounded — because that is what the ratchet compares against. The v8 text summary TRUNCATES instead, so it prints functions as 86.91 where the gate computes 86.92 (392/451 = 86.9179…). Both numbers are correct about different conventions; the gate's is authoritative here because the gate is what enforces. This is the same discrepancy coverage-baseline.backend.json records for its own tier, and it is written down again rather than left for the next reader to rediscover as a defect.
globalNote: Every floor sits BELOW its own measurement, deliberately. A floor recorded AT the run that produced it is a transcript, not a guard: the very next commit moves it, and the gate can only ever report what already happened. Headroom is 1.00 pp on lines and statements (79.45 -> 78.45), 1.50 pp on functions (86.92 -> 85.42) and 1.50 pp on branches (87.00 -> 85.50). Functions and branches get more because they are coarse — 451 functions means one function is 0.22 pp, so a 1.00 pp band is four functions of churn — while 1.00 pp of lines is 111 lines of an 11,145-line denominator.
whatTheHeadroomGuarantees: With the 0.5 pp tolerance on top, the gate trips on: a net loss of more than 167 covered LINES, more than 9 covered FUNCTIONS, or more than 36 covered BRANCHES, at a constant denominator. Those are the bounds the numbers actually enforce, stated as bounds rather than as a slogan about deleting a file.
denominatorTrapNote: KNOWN TRAP, recorded because this project has already been bitten by it: a coverage percentage can FALL because v8 newly ENTERS code that was previously never loaded, so the module joins the denominator carrying its uncovered lines with it. `coverage.all` is true in apps/web/vitest.config.ts precisely so that cannot happen silently — every file matching the include list is already in the denominator whether a test imports it or not. If a metric still falls, cover the code. Never lower these numbers to make a run pass, and never raise them from a local measurement.
touchedFileNote: The exemption is for the ROUTE tier only, and it is temporary rather than principled. `apps/web/src/app/[locale]/(dashboard)/**` is at 7.62% line coverage (162/2125 across 26 files) — async React Server Components that no test currently renders. A 60% touched-file floor over them would refuse every pull request that edits a page, for a gap this establishment run is RECORDING rather than fixing. It is NOT a claim that a route cannot be unit-tested; those files are deliberately still inside the measurement (see the exclusion comment in apps/web/vitest.config.ts), they simply carry their zeros in the global number instead of blocking unrelated work. Remove this prefix once the route tier is covered.

knownGaps.why: Async React Server Components. Nothing in the unit tier renders them, so the permission branch, the notFound() guard and the failed-catalogue fallback in each page are exercised only by the browser tier — which is a different tier with a different failure mode. No critical-module floor is set here on purpose: a floor at 7% would ratify the gap by writing it into the enforcement layer.
knownGaps.closedBy: rendering the page functions in the dom project, or moving their decision logic into a covered module

knownGaps.why: Two library modules with no test at all. They are the honest weak spot of this tier and are recorded rather than excluded. Note the consequence: they are NOT under the touched-file exemption, so a pull request that edits either is refused by the 60% touched-file floor until it carries a test. That is the gate working, not a fault to pre-empt.

criticalModules.why: the customer create, profile, governance and duplicate-review screens and the server actions behind them; P1-27 shipped ten canonical writes with a route, a permission and no screen anybody could reach them from, and this is the code that closed that
VIN entry, duplicate review, documents, history and relations — the surface where a silent wrong write was found by hand while every automated tier was green
every request the browser makes, plus the idempotency table, the read-operation outcome classification and the session cookie; a defect here is wrong for all screens at once
decides which control a reader is shown; WRITE_PERMISSIONS once had zero consumers while ten write forms rendered for anybody
the one module that assembles the CSP; an unsafe-eval or a wildcard source here is the difference between stopping an injected script and not
maps a 422 onto the field that caused it; when this is wrong an operator is told nothing is wrong and the record is not saved
scores and explains a candidate match; an over-confident score merges two customers and P1-OD-017 keeps the merge caller shut precisely because of it
the shared directory contract every CRM read goes through; a keyset cursor defect here drops rows silently, which this repository has already shipped once

criticalModulesNote: Every floor sits below its own recorded measurement, by 5-7 points for the large feature trees and by 5 points for the small single-file ones. `minMatchedFiles` pins how many instrumented files each prefix currently governs: a coverage `include` list narrows SILENTLY, so without this, removing files shrinks what the floor protects while the percentage stays reassuring. coverage-gate.mjs additionally refuses any rule whose prefix matches nothing, so a renamed directory turns the gate red instead of turning the rule off.
